To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the attributes that were rated as high importance and low performance by the nurses were: responsiveness; ease of learning; detail of information; sufficient support; and complete records, accurate records, and records that are never missing.
the attributes of HIS that are most important to nurses' satisfaction and productivity are the quality of the data and the quality of the information provided by the system.
the HIS attributes most important to nurse satisfaction and productivity were ease of learning and responsiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the attributes of a hospital information system (HIS).
the identification of HIS attributes that are important to users' productivity and satisfaction and that are performing poorly.
the evaluation of a HIS implementation and provides insights into how managers can use this evaluation to guide the prioritisation of HIS attributes for intervention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIS was not performing well and needed to be improved.
the most important system attributes to nurses are those related to data quality and system quality.
the HIS attributes most in need of attention are the ones that are important to users and are currently under-performing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIS was not perceived to be performing well on the majority of attributes.
the HIS attributes that have the greatest impact on nurse satisfaction and productivity are system quality, data and information quality, and support services.
the attributes of HIS which have the most impact on nurses are those that are most difficult to implement and maintain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIS evaluation and improvement should be guided by user perceptions of the importance of the HIS attributes to their satisfaction and work performance.
HIS managers should focus their attention on those attributes that are both highly important and poorly performed.
managers should not assume that the most important attributes are also the best performing ones.
